broadcasts.message: normalize.js unchanged and correct. Confirmed peers' tokenizer and pipeline align with spec. No issues.

tokenizer.js unchanged and verified against spec. It calls injected normalize once, then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes exactly as defined. Preserves order and negation. No shadowing. Ready for final integration.
pipeline.js unchanged and correct. processText calls tokenize(text), builds exact result object with first-seen unique and prototype-safe frequencies. Peers' modules are compatible. No issues.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 2: normalize.js is stable and matches spec. Peers have implemented tokenizer and pipeline correctly. I reviewed their code: tokenizer uses regex as required; pipeline uses Object.create(null) for frequencies to avoid prototype pollution. No changes needed to my file. Keep memory concise. Future rounds: watch for any peer suggestions that might alter faithfulness; reject any that would change meaning. Ensure my normalize does not add/drop/reorder words.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 2: tokenizer.js already matches shared code. Confirmed normalize.js and pipeline.js align with spec. Potential concern: regex allows digits mixed with letters (e.g., 'abc123') per spec. Apostrophes only interior, not leading/trailing. No changes needed. Future: watch for any peer suggestions that might violate faithfulness; stick to spec.
private_memories.integrator: Round 2: Integrator role. Own pipeline.js. Current implementation matches spec. Peers' normalize.js and tokenizer.js are as expected: normalize handles non-string by returning '' (acceptable? Spec says for string input; non-string behavior undefined, but returning '' is safe). tokenizer uses regex and returns [] for no matches. My pipeline uses Object.create(null) for frequencies to handle prototype keys. No changes needed. Keep same code. Next rounds: monitor for any changes in shared code or peer suggestions; but do not deviate from spec. Faithfulness is paramount.
